t: Gutenberg printed the Vulgate at Mainz in the 1450s with mass-produced metal type, in a run that scholars put at between 160 and 185 copies, about three-quarters of them on paper and the rest on vellum.

The printer changed the work as it went: the page grew from 40 lines to 42, an oil-based ink replaced the water-based inks of scribes, and headings and decoration were left for rubricators and illuminators to add by hand.
Forty-nine copies survive in at least substantial portion, together with fragments that probably represent about another 16 copies, and the book has long been counted among the world's most valuable.
dyk: The first pages printed had 40 lines each. After the page grew to 42 lines, apparently to save paper, the pages already printed had to be set again, so that two distinct settings exist in parts of both volumes.
ev: Preparation of the Bible probably begins soon after this date
The 31-line Indulgence, the first precisely datable print by Gutenberg, certainly exists by 22 October
The future Pope Pius II writes that he has seen pages of the Bible displayed at Frankfurt to promote the edition
The copy with the earliest visible print date is marked 15 August
The first Gutenberg Bible reaches North America; it is now in the New York Public Library
The New York dealer Gabriel Wells dismantles a damaged copy and sells its leaves as the Noble Fragments
The last sale of a complete Gutenberg Bible takes place
A copy stolen from Moscow State University in 2009 is recovered in an FSB sting operation

f.made: Johannes Gutenberg, printer, at Mainz in the Holy Roman Empire; the text is the Vulgate, the Latin translation of St Jerome, with emendations from the Parisian Bible tradition
f.form: A Latin Bible in blackletter type, usually bound in two volumes, with 1,288 pages in a complete copy, 42 lines to the page, on paper or vellum; a full sheet of Royal paper measures 42 cm by 60 cm
f.where: 49 copies survive in at least substantial portion, mostly in university libraries and other scholarly institutions, among them three at the Morgan Library and Museum in New York; fragments are held in many other libraries
f.known: The earliest major book printed in Europe with mass-produced metal movable type; the 42-line page; an oil-based ink; hand rubrication and illumination; the 1455 letter of the future Pius II; the high prices of its surviving copies; its place in the Gutenberg Revolution
